subject: ACME — pricing & context-length profiling follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & context-length profiling — next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can size pricing options accurately:

Summary from our discovery:
- Primary product: contextual assistance (agent-style) for customer support and internal search.
- Typical UX: user prompt + retrieval + model completion (often multi-turn).
- Initial pilot target: focused on web + mobile support; potential company-wide expansion in Q4.

Numbers we discussed (please confirm):
- Avg prompt tokens per request: ~1.2k
- Avg completion tokens per response: ~600
- % of requests requiring >8k context: ~30%
- % requiring ~32k context: ~25%
- % requiring ~128k context: ~5% (very long doc retrievals)
- Expected monthly volume (combined prompt+completion tokens): ~225M tokens/month
- Target unit economics you mentioned: ideally <= $15 / 1M tokens for pilot

What we need from you to finalize a tailored quote:
1) Confirm the avg prompt/completion numbers above (or send CSV sample).
2) Confirm expected monthly token volume or expected spike windows (daily peak qps).
3) Any hard constraints on budget or procurement timeline.

Attached: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf (pricing bands + context surcharges) — I also pasted a quick example calc below so we're aligned.

Example cost at $12 / 1M tokens:
- 225M tokens = 225 * $12 = $2,700 / month (pilot estimate; context-length surcharges may apply for 32k/128k requests)

Next steps: once you confirm the numbers we can: (a) propose a pilot commitment with an estimated monthly cost and SLA, (b) recommend Dedicated capacity if you want predictable latency for high 32k/128k usage, or (c) stay on hosted with rate-based fallbacks.

Thanks — I can get a formal quote ready by end of day Friday if you confirm the numbers.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Samir Gupta <samir@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & context-length profiling — next steps

Thanks Marissa — good summary. Confirming the numbers from our side (these are estimates based on the last 60 days of traffic):
- Avg prompt tokens: 1,200 (median ~900)
- Avg completion tokens: 600 (median ~450)
- Monthly volume: roughly 225M tokens (75M prompt / 150M completion) — peak days up to 12M tokens
- Context distribution: ~30% <=8k, ~25% 8k-32k, ~5% >32k (of that ~5%, about half are 128k-length ops for deep-document retrievals)
- Preferred target: <= $15 / 1M tokens for pilot (procurement will sign off at or under this)

I attached a usage CSV: acme_usage_profile_202605.csv with a sample window. For billing/approvals we also need a plain-line estimate for a three-month pilot and the canary plan (if we bust the 32k/128k usage how does Redwood bill or fallback?).

Also: our security team asked about data retention and KV caching behavior for long contexts — can you replicate the storage/retention detail in the quote?

Best,
Samir
Samir Gupta
VP, Platform Engineering — Acme Corp
samir@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-05T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & context-length profiling — next steps

Appreciate the quick reply and the CSV, Samir — that helps a lot. A few follow-ups and clarifications from our side:

1) Billing model and quick math (pilot):
- Base token price band examples (hosted API): $12 / 1M tokens (volume tier 0), $9 / 1M tokens (volume tier 1 >1B tokens), $7 / 1M (committed Dedicated pricing).
- Context-length surcharge: additional $3 / 1M tokens for requests that require 32k context, $8 / 1M for 128k requests (this is to cover extra memory and routing costs). Surcharges apply only to the tokens in the completion portion for the affected requests.
- Using your 225M estimate and the distribution you sent: rough pilot E = base_cost + surcharge_cost. Example (base $12 / 1M): base = 225 * $12 = $2,700; surcharge estimate = (25% * 225M * $3/1M) + (5% * 225M * $8/1M) = (56.25 * 3) + (11.25 * 8) = $168.75 + $90 = ~$259 (so pilot est ~ $2,960 / month).

2) Data retention & KV caching:
- By default we keep ephemeral KV cache for 24 hours for improving latency; we can disable caching for PHI/regulated flows. Long-context blobs used for retrieval are not stored beyond retention policies you select — we can include SOC2-aligned retention options in the quote and state them in the contract.

3) Billing behavior on spike / fallback:
- Hosted: if you spike into 32k/128k and you’re in a hosted plan, we allow burst capacity but will flag for overage or suggest short-term Dedicated ramp if sustained. Overage invoices are at the same published rates + a 10% spike handling fee unless you have a committed tier.
- Dedicated: predictable pricing and no surprise overage for committed capacity; if you exceed committed qps, auto-burst is optional with pre-negotiated rates.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll put together a 3-month pilot quote (detailed cost table + retention options + SLA) and share a Doc link by EOD tomorrow.
- Jordan (cc’d) can propose a technical kickoff cadence and a canary plan outline.

Jordan — can you propose a 2-week canary plan that validates latency for 32k/128k requests and an escalation path to Dedicated if we see persistent tail latency?

Thanks — I’ll include the sample math above in the quote so procurement has a single-line estimate.

—Marissa

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-05T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & context-length profiling — next steps

Samir / Marissa — I’ll take this. Proposed canary in two phases:
Phase 1 (1 week): 1% of traffic routed to Redwood hosted with increased tracing and timeout guardrails. Validate latency distribution for 8k/32k requests; ensure median and 95th p95 meet your targets.
Phase 2 (1 week): 5% traffic + synthetic load testing for 32k/128k windows. If 95th p95 tail latency > target or errors >0.5%, trigger a short Dedicated ramp for the canary period.

I’ll draft a technical checklist and a small runbook for failure modes (fallback to shorter-context model variant, retry jitter). Will share by tomorrow AM.

—Jordan

Sounds good — procurement is fine with the pilot estimate up to $12k for three months (covers pilot + buffers). Please send the formal quote and the retention language and we’ll route for signatures.
